conclusion.oneLine: The fifth repair's exact-goal handoff is CORRECTLY REFUSED at COMMON vertex 3 because the 0.6 signed corner overshoot pushes the capsule footprint onto a water column at (-46, ., 16); the navigator therefore keeps the snapped cell centre (-44, 52.85, 16) as the steering target, and the closest approach to the published goal while steering is live is 0.4356 > arriveRadius 0.35 — unsatisfiable, exactly the CG-IMPL-010 shape, with a safety refusal rather than pure arithmetic as its cause.

mechanism.claim: Tangential goal-to-steer-target distance is 0.6356 (not 0.6): the local up is tilted -0.0198 in x, and discarding the normal component of the 1.8-unit convention gap between the authored foot goal 51.05 and the clearance-carrying waypoint 52.85 injects an extra 0.0357 of TANGENTIAL offset along the tilt. Closest approach while steering is 0.6356 - 0.2 = 0.4356 > 0.35.

mechanism.claim: The measured pose corroborates the model exactly: body is 0.1777 from the snapped vertex (< dead zone 0.2), 0.7598 from the published goal (> 0.35), and terraUnits 5.845337 is 0.154663 short of the 6 walked units that vertex 3 represents — the same shortfall as the body's own x offset from -44.

mechanism.claim: vertexReached at a turning vertex requires along >= 0, i.e. the body must physically cross the x = -44 plane. Parked at x = -43.845 it never does, so railCursor never advances and no further goal is ever published. Zero nudges and stillTime 0 are consistent: the stuck watchdog only counts stillness while a control is pushing, and the navigator issues none.
mechanism.source: main/src/story/commonGroundDirector.ts vertexReached; integration-navigation-repair-report.md section 1 (same disarm argument)

commonVsSurvey.finding: This is NOT a sign/negative-axis, quantization or parity asymmetry. Every SURVEY (CG_ROUTE_LONG) turn vertex, including the negative-x overshoots at -28.6, -30.6, -32.6 and -42.6, certifies its footprint column and takes the handoff (closest approach 0.0, arrival satisfiable). The COMMON polyline is simply authored closer to unsafe landform at its western end.

commonVerticesFailing.cause: planet face edge / edge margin at cell (-25,9) — x = -50 is the planetSize-50 face boundary; column is dry solid but not traversable

commonVerticesFailing.note: TERMINAL vertex C: overshoot comes from RailRouteOptions.terminalOvershoot = CG_RAIL_CORNER_OVERSHOOT, and there is no outgoing leg to redirect it along.

commonVsSurvey.consequence: Terra stalls at vertex 3 first. Even if vertex 3 were made reachable, vertices 6 and 9 stall next. Three of the COMMON rail's published goals are unsatisfiable on this world.

'footprint-not-certified' and 'footprint-height-mismatch' at (-46,.,16), (-50,.,18) and (-48,.,10) must remain REFUSALS in any future test fixture — they are the water/face-edge guard working.
The existing refusal tests (goal-substituted-for-safety, water-leg, goal-outside-terminal-cell, footprint-height-mismatch) must stay unchanged.

railImplementationVsAuthoredGeometry.verdict: BOTH are implicated; a rail-only correction is provably insufficient at the terminal vertex.
railImplementationVsAuthoredGeometry.railSide: At turning vertices 3 and 6 the overshoot direction is the INCOMING leg direction. An overshoot taken along the OUTGOING leg instead would still satisfy vertexReached (along = 0.6 * (in.out) = 0 >= 0 at a right-angle turn, distance 0.6 <= arrive+0.6+1) while landing the footprint on the route's own next cell, which certifies. This is a rail-implementation option and is stated as an OBSERVATION, not a proposed repair.
railImplementationVsAuthoredGeometry.geometrySide: At vertex 9 (C, the terminal) there is no outgoing leg; RailRouteOptions.terminalOvershoot points south into the water column (-48, ., 10). No choice of overshoot DIRECTION exists there. Either the terminal-overshoot device or the authored placement of C / the western end of CG_ROUTE_COMMON must change. Any such change is a creative-geometry decision (the 18-unit signed physical span, the 8 units outside the fixed reference and the E-C six-unit separation are load-bearing), and belongs to the Chapter Director, not to this audit.
railImplementationVsAuthoredGeometry.authorization: None. Root must review before any seventh material repair.
